label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (insecure-randomness) is TP: java.util.Random.nextGaussian() produces non-cryptographically secure values used for session tokens (rememberMeKey). OWASP explicitly recommends against using standard Random for security-sensitive operations. Alert 2 (XSS) is FP: user input from request parameters never reaches the response writer—the 'user' variable is always "Gayle" plus hardcoded class suffix, making it constant. Cookie name/value are also hardcoded/not user-controllable.

evidence.note: Random.nextGaussian() used for rememberMeKey generation—insecure for security tokens
user variable assigned constant "Gayle" plus hardcoded class suffix—never user-controllable
